The simulation uses OpenFOAM reactingParcelFoam solver in a 2D axisymmetric setup.
The domain is a rectangle in the axial-radial plane with axial length 0.2 m and radius 0.05 m.
The mesh has 100 axial cells and 50 radial cells, graded finer near the axis and the injector face.
Use blockMesh to generate the axisymmetric wedge mesh representing the cylindrical chamber.
The initial air in the chamber is at rest, T = 800 K, p = 101325 Pa, with mass fractions O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767.
The inlet co-flow air has U = (10 0 0) m/s, T = 800 K, p = 101325 Pa, with the same O2 and N2 mass fractions.
Derive inlet k and epsilon from a turbulence intensity of 5%.
Walls are no-slip with fixed temperature 400 K.
The outlet uses totalPressure at approximately 101325 Pa and zero gradient for all other variables.
Use the k-epsilon turbulence model.
Use the reactingParcelFoam Lagrangian spray solver with the standard drag model and RanzMarshall heat and mass transfer model.
The fuel is liquid n-dodecane, nC12H26.
Inject the spray at the center of the inlet face.
Use the cone injection model with a half-angle of 30 degrees and injection velocity of 10 m/s as an assumption.
The liquid mass flow rate is 0.002 kg/s.
The droplet injection temperature is 300 K.
Use a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m.
Inject continuously from t = 0 until the end of the simulation at 0.05 s as an assumption.
Use a two-step global gas-phase reaction mechanism for n-dodecane combustion, with janaf thermodynamics and reasonable Arrhenius rate parameters.
The total simulation time is 0.05 s.
Document all assumed parameters, including injection velocity, cone half-angle, injection duration, and reaction rate constants, as engineering assumptions.
